README: The customer-text guard's LANGUAGE, as data (`scripts/customer_text_guard.py` keeps the machinery).
THE RULE. A customer artifact says the verdict and the findings about the customer's AGENT. It never says how
OUR pipeline reached them: audit / judge / harness / suite internals, coverage holes, template caveats about
features we have not shipped, or repair items for our own SDK / plugin. Plain technical words about the agent
are fine: this is not a jargon ban, so a term belongs here only when it names our machinery.
SHAPES. `terms[]`: `id` (stable, quoted in every violation), `class` (one of `classes`), `pattern` (a Python
regex, case-insensitive unless `case_sensitive`), `artifacts` (the `artifacts` kinds it applies to; absent =
every kind), `say_instead` (the rewrite the violation asks for), `unless_line` (optional regex, case-insensitive: a line it matches is

the term's sanctioned use), `unless_block` (optional regex, case-insensitive: a line it matches opens a block that is the term's sanctioned use, the bullet lines that follow it, e.g. the "Done so far" list of a stop message, whose lines name what exists with its id). `artifacts{}`: kind -> {path?, reader, under?}; `under: scored_run` reads the path in the
scored run's dir and each of its trial dirs; a kind with no `path` is read only from the text handed in (`final_chat`: the hand-off
message, checked by hooks/report_guard.py); `report_page` reads every prose text the filled page embeds but the files its `skip`
names: transcripts (the agent's and the simulated user's own words), the eval set's judge-facing rubric (evals.md is its
customer rendering, read as `evals_md`), the scenario files that are the customer's voice or world (the persona, the
opening line, the agent's context, the starting and final records), and verdicts.json, the graders' record: the judge's
words, the agent's words it quotes, and the fixed correction sentence code writes into it (`verdict_corrections.py`:
`CORRECTION_REASONS` plus the audit row's clause, tested at its writer; in practice no free text of ours is rendered from it).
The audit's own note under `audit_corrected` never reaches the page: the fill's schema ships it as `{quote_turn}` only.
`skip_fields`: per embedded path, the keys whose values
are the customer's voice or world: the persona, the simulated user's lines, verbatim turns and quotes, the agent's call args.
Every other value in those files is ours (narrative text, our mock's replies) and stays checked.
`regression_rows` (`auto_regressions`): the titles and reasons of the page's regressions lists, read from the page's copy
(`regressions.page_copy`) whether or not the text is handed in: the plan on disk keeps operator reasons the page never shows.
`internal_fields`: field lines of agent_findings.md that feed our own loop or grade our own certainty; the page copy drops them, so the
guard skips them. `fixes_md`: the structural rule — a fixes.md section homed to one of `internal_homes`, or a
heading matching `internal_headings`, belongs in `internal_file`.
Add a term with the offending line it was cut from (a test fixture), never a guessed one.
internal_fields: what the suite does about it

terms.say_instead: say what the agent did, with the quote that shows it
name the run and the conversation, not the review step that read it
describe the user's move in plain words
state the agent's behaviour itself
say 'the starting data' or name the records
drop it: how the test harness changed is internal
drop it: how a check was tuned is internal
drop the sentence: it describes a feature, not this agent
state the verdict only

terms.pattern: \bnot tested here\b|\breached by too few conversations\b|\btoo few conversations to count\b
terms.say_instead: drop it: a gap in the suite's own coverage is closed or tracked internally

terms.pattern: \b(?:passes|failures) are not evidence\b|\bnot yet shown able to (?:fail|pass)\b
terms.say_instead: drop it: a check's own standing is internal
move it to the internal file: a repair of our own tooling is not the customer's fix
move it to the internal file
never name our settings: say what the customer does
name the scenario as the report does (`scenario_01`), never its folder id
say the verdict and its reason in words, as the Agent line does: "Don't ship", "a critical failure", "failed a required check" — never the scores block's token
a fault a re-run answers is re-run, never sent to /edit-env

terms.pattern: \bnot counted against your agent\b|\brests on a defect in the simulation\b
terms.say_instead: drop it: whether a check counts is decided once (release_verdict.json suite_defects) and the results show it
drop it: how the simulation reaches a model is ours; say what the agent did
say what the agent did, with the quote that shows it
name the run as the report does, never the step of ours that ran it
say only the stop text, nothing before it
drop the id: name the run or the scenario as the report does
drop the line: what the suite did about a limitation is internal

terms.pattern: \bcould not be proven by a test\b
terms.say_instead: drop it: a check's own standing is internal (release_verdict.json banner, not customer_banner)
drop it: the eval set's revision is run.json's (internal)
name the commit only: whether the agent's source differs from it is run.json agent_source (internal)
drop it: how sure we are of our own measurement is internal (run.json); state the result
drop it: say the count, or nothing; how exact our count is stays internal
drop the caveat: say which trials passed and which failed
drop it: what the suite did not re-check is closed in the loop or tracked internally
drop the remedy: what the simulation carries is the scan's to seed, not the customer's to add
